```
rtk cargo test -p session-worktree-provision --no-run
rtk cargo test -p session-worktree-provision
rtk cargo build -p worktree-ctl
rtk cargo test -p worktree-ctl
```

`worktree-ctl` must still build and remain at **10 passed / 15 failed** — you are not implementing `new` in this unit, only unblocking it.

## Hard constraints

- **Scope is `memory-api/crates/session-worktree-provision/` only.** Do NOT implement any `worktree-ctl` subcommand. Do NOT modify `tools/worktree/worktree-ctl/**` — not even the stubs.
- Do NOT modify `tools/worktree/worktree.sh` or `tools/worktree/tests/**`.
- Do NOT touch `session-capture-hook` or `session-workspace-resolver`.
- Do NOT change existing provisioning behavior, thresholds, or defaults (`WORKTREE_MAX` 8, `WORKTREE_IDLE_SECS` 86400, `WORKTREE_STALE_SECS` 14400).

- Do NOT stage, revert, `git checkout --`, `git restore`, `git stash`, or `git clean` anything in the real repo — note the irony: your *tests* may stash inside temp fixtures, but never in a real checkout.
- Tests must use temp fixtures only, never the real repository.
- **One retry cap**: if validation fails twice, STOP and report verbatim. Never leave the crate non-compiling — a previous attempt at this crate left an unclosed delimiter and had to be reverted, so prefer small surgical edits and re-check compilation as you go.

```
stash API: <signature, verbatim> -> <subprocess write used | read mechanism used>
```

The epic is committed and durable — submodule `03b93e34`, superproject `bf048f5e`, `e94d4e8c`, `f5708fe7`, pre-commit hook passed, no unrelated files swept in.

## Delivered

**Ticket `5e6cf4f8` — worktree-ctl rewrite: complete.** All eight subcommands (`new`, `list`, `rebase`, `merge`, `remove`, `rename`, `finish`, `doctor`) implemented with `--dry-run` throughout. **28 tests passing** (10 parse + 15 ported lifecycle contracts + 3 maintenance); `session-worktree-provision` extended with a shared reclaim-eligibility API at **35 passing**. `worktree.sh` and the shell harness are deleted, with 11 docs plus spec `585aa074` updated.

**A `main`-breaking regression found and fixed.** `session-capture-hook` was at 3/12 on `main`. Ticket `0afe45b5`'s commit `184b8e5e` let write paths bypass `require_mutation_target`, and — more seriously — misclassified genuine worktree invocations as the main checkout, which would have blocked real agents' writes in real worktrees. Fixed to 32/0 on its branch.

## Two things need you

**1. `main` is still broken — the submodule histories diverged.** The fix cannot merge: `8fdcf090` (the gitlink `main` records) is **not** an ancestor of `memory-api`'s `main` tip. An earlier agent fast-forwarded the submodule's `main` onto the feature line, which does not contain `main`'s recorded submodule history. The ancestry gate caught this and refused rather than silently dropping history. Resolving it needs a real merge inside `memory-api` — reconciling `8fdcf090` and `1fe5c148` — which is a judgement call about submodule history I won't make unilaterally.

**2. Branch `agent/5e6cf4f8-worktree-ctl` is ready to integrate** but I'd hold it until the divergence above is settled, since both touch `memory-api`.

## Process failures worth recording

- **I parallelized S1 and S2 into the same build graph.** Disjoint files, shared dependency — S1's broken `policy.rs` blocked S2's validation. Overlapping build scope is overlapping scope.
- **Sub-agents' shell cwd is unstable**, sometimes the worktree, sometimes the main checkout on `main`. Three agents ran in the wrong tree; two produced actively misleading results before one caught it. Every git-sensitive prompt now needs an explicit `cd` plus verification.
- **I over-constrained the write allowlist twice**, blocking S4 (stash) and S5 (`git rebase`). Both workers correctly refused to proceed rather than quietly breaching the boundary.
- **Validation scoping caused the original regression**: `0afe45b5` validated only `mcp-toolmon`, never the crate consuming the behavior it changed.

Also noted: 10 worktrees exist against `WORKTREE_MAX` of 8, so automatic provisioning will hit `CapReached`; and ticket `33463861` now carries the `session_check_in` fresh-worktree gap, which the guard misclassification likely explains.
